title: Hosted Chat + Streaming + Function Calling: Enterprise Triage & Prioritization Playbook
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Create an operational triage and prioritization playbook for inbound enterprise feature requests for Hosted API chat/streaming/function-calling/structured-output. Aim: reduce time-to-decision, capture unmet enterprise requirements (SLA, audit/KMS, VPC routing, deterministic structured outputs), and produce a prioritized backlog with clear trade-offs for runtime, reliability, and cost. This ticket will inventory recent enterprise asks, define scoring criteria, run two intake sessions with sales/solutions-engineering, and produce a recommended roadmap and handoff to Eng/Design for scoping.
acceptance_criteria: A documented scoring rubric that balances security/compliance, revenue urgency, engineering effort, and customer reach
Intake notes from two sessions with Sales/SE (at least 8 enterprise requests recorded)
A prioritized list of top 6 candidate features with recommended release tier: Quick Win / Mid-term / Requires Private/Dedicated
Clear non-functional requirements per candidate (SLO targets, audit retention, KMS/HSM needs, anonymization requirements)
Handoff artifact (PRD stub + engineering spike tickets) created and linked
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Kapoor: Kickoff — collecting initial enterprise requests from account teams (EMEA and NA). Noted repeated asks: streaming stability under high-concurrency, function-calling auth delegation, structured JSON schema enforcement for regulatory outputs.

2026-03-11 Ethan Chen: Met with Solutions Eng (Ana M. and Leo R.). Logged 9 discrete requests. Flagged two enterprise customers requiring SOC2 + customer-managed KMS for any function-calling flows — probably blocks Hosted tier unless we add envelope encryption.

2026-03-12 Sofia Martinez (Sales): Customer A (fintech) will consider Dedicated if we can guarantee 99.95% inference availability and 10ms p50 generation for short chat messages — otherwise they will self-host. Put them as high-revenue qualifying lead.

2026-03-12 Priya Kapoor: Drafted initial scoring weights (security 30%, revenue 25%, implementation effort inverse 20%, cross-customer reach 15%, latency/cost impact 10%). Will iterate in intake session.

2026-03-13 Ethan Chen: Internal sync with Eng leads. Eng asks to separate streaming stability fixes (runtime-level) from protocol-level features (chunked function-calls, reconnect semantics). Recommended creating separate ENG spikes for runtime kernel scheduling and client-side reconnect strategies.
decisions: 2026-03-13 Decision: Use a two-axis scoring matrix for prioritization: Enterprise-constraints (security/compliance/blockers) vs. Business-opportunity (ARR/expansion). This prevents high-revenue-but-blocked items from being deprioritized incorrectly.

2026-03-13 Decision: Any feature that requires customer-managed KMS or private network routing will default to 'Requires Private/Dedicated' unless an envelope-encryption shim can be scoped as low-effort.

2026-03-13 Decision: Structured output enforcement (strong JSON schema validation + deterministic failure modes) to be trialed as a hosted beta under 'structured-output-stability' flag to gather regression data before a broader rollout.
next_steps: Run two 60-minute intake workshops (2026-03-15 and 2026-03-17) with Sales, SE, and Support to validate and augment request list
Apply scoring rubric to each request and produce candidate backlog (due 2026-03-19)
Create PRD stubs for top 3 items and generate ENG spike tickets: ENG-7102 (streaming reliability), ENG-7103 (function-calling auth model), ENG-7104 (structured-output validation)
Coordinate with Security to scope KMS/HSM options and list gating requirements for Hosted vs Dedicated
Schedule cross-functional review (Product/Eng/Design/Security) for 2026-03-20 to approve handoff
